newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest-July 29.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest-July 29.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media & the Internet and Brand-name Products.
ADVERTISING, MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - German telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom declares an advertising victory at the Tour de France, where the team it sponsored not only won the race but invaluable worldwide publicity. Telekom spokesman Ulrich Lissek says Telekom's brand-name recognition reached about 96 percent in Germany through its sponsorship of the cyclists. (Reuter)

PARIS - French pay television group Canal Plus says it is suing the French terrestrial television channels and their media-selling units over their refusal to accept an advert promoting Canal Plus last April. (Reuter)

ROME - Major television broadcasters and media groups operating in Italy says they have reached a preliminary deal to create a single digital television platform. The deal involves Berlusconi's Mediaset, state broadcaster RAI, Telecom Italia and France's Canal Plus together with its majority-owned Italian pay-TV unit, Telepiu. (Reuter)

PARIS - Advertising agency Loeb et Associes runs the launch campaign for Perrier-Vittel's new soft drink, Fu. It represents a new step for the mineral water company, which so far has only diversified by putting orange and lemon flavours in its bottled water. (Le Figaro)
PARIS - The international satellite organisation Eutelsat says it bought the TDF2 satellite from Telediffusion de France, a unit of France Telecom.
(Reuter)
PARIS - Top model Claudia Schiffer seeks damages from Paris Match and Voici and denies allegations carried in the magazines over her liaison with magician David Copperfield. (Liberation)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - The chairman of state-owned airline Air France, Christian Blanc, briefs Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on the situation at the flag carrier but gives no details on any hopes of an early privatisation.
(Reuter).
PARIS - Air France plans to cut its Paris-Teheran flight from September 14. (La Tribune)

LONDON - Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods company LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton, visited major shareholders in Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc on Monday, industry sources say.
Arnault plans to return to London Thursday to see more shareholders, seeking their backing for his proposal for the break up of Guinness and GrandMet. (Reuter)

LONDON - NTT, the $160 billion Japanese telecoms titan, is focusing European investment plans on second carriers in the key markets of France and Germany, says Shuji Tomita, managing director of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's European operations. NTT might invest in a company like France's Cegetel, which has ambitions to establish a pan-European network, or in telephone operators on a country-by-country basis, he says. (Reuter)

PARIS - French pharmaceutical firm Sanofi wants to sell its stake in Nina Ricci perfumes, daily newspaper La Tribune says. Sanofi holds 49.9 percent of Nina Ricci's capital directly and 56.5 percent indirectly, with the rest belonging to Nina Ricci's chairman and his family. (Reuter)
PARIS - French domestic appliance maker Moulinex plans to cut back its microwave oven-making capacity because of competition, notably from South Korea's Daewoo. (Les Echos)
